findings.title: Authorization uses tx.origin
findings.message: tx.origin participates in a condition that can gate execution.
findings.remediation: Use msg.sender with an explicit role or ownership check, then add an access-control test.

findings.title: State write follows an external call
findings.message: An address low-level call precedes a write to this contract's storage in the same function.
findings.remediation: Apply checks-effects-interactions and verify a reentrancy guard with a local regression test.

findings.title: Low-level call result is not checked
findings.message: An address call/delegatecall/staticcall result is discarded, or its captured success flag is unused.
findings.remediation: Capture and enforce the success flag, or explicitly return it to a caller that handles failure.

findings.title: Ether send result is discarded
findings.message: The boolean from an address send operation is discarded.
findings.remediation: Handle failed delivery explicitly; prefer a pull-payment design when recipients can reject Ether.

findings.title: Caller controls a delegatecall target
findings.message: An externally callable function contains delegation to a caller-derived target without a recognized local caller restriction.
findings.remediation: Use a trusted implementation target and enforce the intended caller/upgrade policy before delegation.

findings.title: Selfdestruct lacks a local caller restriction
findings.message: An externally callable function contains selfdestruct without a recognized local caller restriction.
findings.remediation: Remove the operation or enforce the intended caller policy and test unauthorized calls locally.

findings.title: Loop repeatedly credits the full msg.value
findings.message: A loop writes the whole msg.value into storage on each iteration.
findings.remediation: Compute and validate a per-item allocation before the loop, or require a single recipient per payment.

related.label: Repeated accounting operation
related.excerpt: for (uint256 i; i < recipients.length; i++) { credits[recipients[i]] += msg.value; }

findings.title: Block-derived array selection
findings.message: A block-derived value is used in modulo arithmetic to choose an array index.
findings.remediation: Use an appropriate verifiable randomness or commit/reveal design with an explicit adversary model.

findings.title: Packed hash combines dynamic inputs
findings.message: A hash uses packed encoding of two or more locally resolved string/bytes values, leaving input boundaries ambiguous.
findings.remediation: Use abi.encode with explicit types and domain separation for the intended hash or signature protocol.

findings.title: Token operation boolean is discarded
findings.message: A transfer/transferFrom/approve operation declared to return bool is used without its result.
findings.remediation: Use a compatible SafeERC20 wrapper or enforce the token's return value and test failure behavior.

related.label: Resolved boolean-returning interface method
related.excerpt: function transfer(address to, uint256 amount) external returns(bool);

findings.title: Strict equality on contract Ether balance
findings.message: A condition requires this contract's Ether balance to equal an exact value.
findings.remediation: Track internal accounting explicitly and avoid relying on an exact external Ether balance.

findings.title: Reverting Ether transfer inside a loop
findings.message: A payable-address transfer in a loop lets a rejecting recipient revert the whole batch.
findings.remediation: Use independently claimable payments or isolate recipient failures without losing accounting correctness.

related.label: Enclosing batch loop
related.excerpt: for (uint256 i; i < recipients.length; i++) { recipients[i].transfer(1); }
